title: Record one canonical owner per duplicated function in the ownership map, and fail the unit suite on an unrecorded second implementation
problem: At base b1950be2 (#196's head when the unit started), eight functions on GREG's mission path had two or more implementations and no file named which one was canonical: temporary teams, commerce closure, the goal runtime, the status evidence ladder, autonomy levels, regression closing, organ exchange and inbox transport. Nothing stopped another implementation from landing unrecorded, and the program's open and planned work adds more: #235's greg/autonomy.py, WU-03 greg/teams.py, WU-06 nodes.py, WU-12 greg/regressions.py and WU-13 governance/reality_ladder.py. Directive section 52 asks, for every major mechanism, for the canonical implementation, alternatives, shims, experiments, benchmarks, historical implementations, migration path and retirement condition, and says 'Do not allow architectural generations to remain equally canonical forever.' Section 3 asks for one canonical persistent mission architecture; section 76 says 'Do not keep obsolete implementations merely to preserve history.'
founder_intent_refs: INTENT-2026-09-30-MASTER-BUILD-DIRECTIVE (section 76, the same governing rule in the original directive)
baseline: b1950be2: docs/collaboration/ARCHITECTURE-OWNERSHIP-MAP.yaml says 'one canonical owner per concern; two active owners is a defect' but records concerns, not functions, and nothing reads it. scripts/ci/check_authority_singleton.py counts authority artifacts only and says it 'does NOT restrict multiple capability implementations'. No test fails when a second implementation of a function lands or when greg/ imports a superseded one.

alternatives.name: Proposed: function_owner_records in the existing ownership map, three static guards and a frozen pin, all in one unit test
alternatives.description: Eight records in a new function_owner_records section of docs/collaboration/ARCHITECTURE-OWNERSHIP-MAP.yaml. Five are CANONICAL, decided by what greg/ and the CLI import and call at b1950be2; three are NEEDS_FOUNDER_DECISION with the evidence on each side, a safe default and a review trigger. tests/unit/test_canonical_owner_guard.py (15 tests) checks: every registered module and qualname exists (ast, nothing imported); no greg module reaches a HISTORICAL or RETIRED alternate through any import form greg uses, including _lazy and module-name string tables, and every unresolvable dynamic import is allowlisted with a reason; no module-level binding in greg, foundry, egregore, omnimorph, autonomy or governance re-implements a registered function by marker, by exact name or by structural copy. PINNED, FOUNDER_DECISIONS and MUST_FLAG freeze the records, entries, canonical module sets and markers. scripts/ci/check_canonical_owner_guard_mutants.py holds 53 mutants.
advantages: Every duplicated function on the mission path has one recorded owner or an explicit NEEDS_FOUNDER_DECISION with evidence on each side
Reuses the repository's existing owner record; no new file format, authority plane or runtime component
Runs in Canonical CI job 1's full suite with no workflow change (about 20 s)
A new candidate, alternate or distinct entry needs no test change, so #235 and the WU units can record themselves
53 of 53 mutants caught; 48 of 48 single-entry deletions caught
disadvantages: Guard 3 is a heuristic: near copies, methods, code outside the six packages and a second implementation inside a listed module pass
The pins live in the test; a diff that edits the YAML and the test together defeats them, visibly
The founder_ruling check cannot authenticate the founder
A 1,140-line test with its own AST resolver joins the review surface
alternatives.revival_evidence: Retained; revisit if a duplicate lands on #196 while the guard passes, or if a runtime capability router becomes the canonical dispatch path.

alternatives.name: Strongest competing design: runtime single-owner dispatch through a capability router or governed module loader

disadvantages: Changes runtime behaviour, which this unit may not do

Section 52 stays unmet, and the three open founder decisions stay scattered across the intent ledger and the conflict matrix instead of next to the code they decide.

No risk of a heuristic false positive
disadvantages: Architectural generations remain equally canonical, which section 52 forbids
A greg import of a superseded implementation is invisible

pass_2.attack_summary: Two reviews of round 1 (77deac50), done by separate agents of this same session (not independent sessions or humans), attacked the guards with probes on synthetic and real trees: one for bypasses, one for fidelity to the scope and the evidence. They reported 16 findings (F1-F9, MUH-F1-MUH-F7), all confirmed; F9 repeats MUH-F3 and MUH-F6, and MUH-F7 repeats F7. Round 2 (66794c5b) fixed every one, each with a regression test that fails on 77deac50, and added 33 mutants that replay them. A final verifier re-ran the guard, the mutants, related suites, both CI scripts and merge checks against #196's current head and eight other refs.

pass_2.final_design: Eight function_owner_records in docs/collaboration/ARCHITECTURE-OWNERSHIP-MAP.yaml: five CANONICAL (temporary teams, commerce closure, regression closing, organ exchange, inbox transport) and three NEEDS_FOUNDER_DECISION (goal runtime, status evidence ladder, autonomy levels), each with migration_path, every alternate with a retirement or revival condition and every undecided record with decision_needed, safe_default and review_trigger. tests/unit/test_canonical_owner_guard.py (15 tests): existence by ast; a greg import guard over every import form greg uses, failing closed on unresolvable dynamic imports; a definition guard over every module-level binding in six packages by marker, exact registered name and structural copy; PINNED, FOUNDER_DECISIONS and MUST_FLAG. scripts/ci/check_canonical_owner_guard_mutants.py: 53 mutants, each naming its test.
